## The usual cause: new references on every render

React compares props with `Object.is` (reference equality) when deciding whether `React.memo` should skip a re-render. If you pass a **function, object, or array literal** as a prop, it's a brand-new reference every time the parent renders — even if the values inside look identical.

```jsx
// New function reference every render
<Child onClick={() => doThing()} />

// New object reference every render
<Child style={{ color: 'red' }} />
```

`onClick !== onClick` from the previous render, so `memo` thinks the prop changed.

## But check this first: is the child even memoized?

Without `React.memo`, a child **always** re-renders when its parent re-renders — regardless of whether props changed at all. This is the most common reason and has nothing to do with prop values.

```jsx
function Child({ name }) { ... }        // re-renders every time Parent renders
export default React.memo(Child)         // now props are compared
```

## Fix checklist, in order

1. Wrap the child: `export default React.memo(Child)`
2. Wrap functions passed as props: `const onClick = useCallback(() => doThing(), [deps])`
3. Wrap objects/arrays passed as props: `const style = useMemo(() => ({ color: 'red' }), [])`
4. If a prop is JSX/children built inline, that's also a new reference each time — lift it out or memoize it too

## Quick way to confirm which one it is

Open React DevTools → Profiler → check "Highlight updates when components render," then look at the child's render reason. It'll tell you if it's "props changed" (reference issue, steps 2-3) or the child isn't memoized at all (step 1).

Next: run the app, open React DevTools Profiler, and check what the child's re-render reason says.
